{"path":"snake_openrouter-deepseek-deepseek-v4.1-flash_01.html","edit_description":"Create a complete single-file classic Snake game in HTML/CSS/JavaScript.

REQUIREMENTS:
- 30x30 grid board rendered with <canvas> (cell size ~20px, canvas 600x600), responsive scaling via CSS max-width.
- Classic snake mechanics: snake moves continuously in one of four directions, grows by 1 when eating food, game ends on wall collision or self collision.
- Keyboard controls: Arrow keys and WASD for player 1. For human vs human mode, player 2 uses arrow keys while player 1 uses WASD (or vice versa) — clearly documented on the start menu.
- Three game modes selectable from a start menu: "Human vs Human", "CPU vs Human", "CPU vs CPU".
- In two-player modes there are TWO snakes on the board, each with its own score and its own food. CPU snakes automatically path-find toward the nearest food using a safe greedy algorithm (BFS/flood-fill to avoid trapping itself and to avoid other snakes' bodies — prefer moves that keep the most open space, avoid reversing direction, avoid walls and all occupied cells).
- A CPU snake must also avoid colliding with the other snake.
- Score displayed live during gameplay for each snake (HUD above/below the canvas showing Player 1 / Player 2 or CPU labels and scores).
- Start menu screen (overlay) with mode buttons and control instructions.
- Game over screen (overlay) showing final scores, winner, and "Press SPACE (or Enter) to restart" plus a key to return to the menu.
- Restart with a keypress (Space/Enter restarts the same mode immediately).
- Also support single-snake classic behavior in Human vs Human / CPU vs Human as appropriate: in "CPU vs Human" mode player is one snake and CPU is the other; in "CPU vs CPU" both are CPU.
- Game ends for a snake when it crashes; in two-player mode, when a snake dies it is removed and the round ends when either both are dead or only one remains — simplest robust rule: round ends when ANY snake crashes, showing the game over screen with both scores and declaring the surviving snake the winner (or draw if both crash simultaneously).
- Use requestAnimationFrame with a fixed tick interval (e.g. 120ms) for smooth continuous movement; CPU decisions evaluated each tick.
- Nice retro/neon styling: dark background, glowing snake bodies, distinct colors for snake 1 (green) and snake 2 (orange/blue), food as red/glowing circles, grid lines subtle.
- Pause with P key.
- All CSS and JS inline in one file. No external dependencies.
- Clean, well-structured, commented JavaScript."}
